question.problem: Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of $(1.1)^{5}$ using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^{5}$ in ascending powers of $x.$ Round your final percentage error to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, 

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{1}{2!}n(n-1){x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{5} & =1+5x+\frac{1}{2!}\cdot 5\cdot 4\cdot {x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n} \\  & =1+5x+10{x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(1+x)}^{5}≈1+5x+10{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute $x=0.1$ into the above approximation of $(1+x)^{5}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(1.1)^{5} & =(1+0.1)^{5} \\  & ≈1+5(0.1)+10(0.1)^{2} \\  & =1+5(0.1)+10(0.01) \\  & =1+0.5+0.1 \\  & =1.6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(1.1)^{5}-1.6|}{(1.1)^{5}}\times 100 \\  & ≈0.65%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
